sentences.text: Flight Data Gateway maintains scheduled flight identifiers, destinations, planned departure times, and revisions needed for baggage planning.
Flight schedules include airline-specific dispatch targets and connection windows, and changes are time-stamped for operational use.
Baggage Control System evaluates flight assignments against current schedule data before accepting bag routing instructions.
The planned dispatch time is the reference for prioritizing bags, while the published departure time remains the passenger-facing schedule value.
Baggage Control System applies cutoff profiles configured for each carrier, flight, and operating condition.
A bag accepted before cutoff retains its assigned flight unless a subsequent schedule or operational change requires reassessment.
When schedule revisions move a departure earlier, Baggage Operations Supervisor reviews affected flights and directs priority adjustments.
Cutoff values account for screening, sortation, make-up, and transfer handling allowances rather than only aircraft departure.
Baggage Control System receives the Flight Cutoff Advisory.
Baggage Control System compares remaining processing time with route-specific handling estimates.
Bags with confirmed screening clearance may proceed to flight-specific sort destinations when capacity is available.
Bags awaiting screening are held from final flight induction even when their scheduled departure is near.
North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner record screening outcomes for inducted bags.
The Image Resolution Desk reviews unresolved images, and final routing remains withheld until disposition is recorded.
A positive threat indication suspends ordinary routing until the authorized security disposition is entered.
Explosives Response Team produces the Custody Seal Log.
When screening disposition is pending, Baggage Control System preserves a recoverable bag-to-flight association rather than releasing the bag to make-up.
Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes eligible bags according to flight assignment and current cutoff priority.
Concourse Zone Controller coordinates induction demand with available conveyor capacity across the operating area.
Induction Tray Conveyor admits bags in priority order, subject to scan confirmation and safe spacing.
East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor receive flight groups according to active allocation rules.
Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit presents bags for outbound loading only after flight grouping and screening status are confirmed.
Outbound Load Control Desk uses planned dispatch time and load-close targets to monitor whether assigned bags can be accepted.
Airline Ramp Coordinator reports changes to loading readiness that could alter the usable cutoff.
Baggage Operations Supervisor may defer lower-priority bags when a flight's remaining processing window is insufficient.
Bags missing the active flight cutoff are held for reassignment or recovery rather than routed into an unavailable departure build.
